subject: Finova SLO & Regional Routing Follow-up / Next Steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finova.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@finova.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Mar 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + next steps (SLOs, routing, residency)

Alex/Priya — thanks again for the discovery call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared starting point for sizing and a POC: 

What we heard from you: 
- Primary product: low-latency chat (streaming tokens) + occasional batch text-generation and embeddings for analytics.
- Latency targets: first-byte for streaming < 300ms p50, p95 target ~650-700ms (global target you mentioned: p95 < 700ms).
- Throughput / concurrency: steady-state ~200-300 concurrent active sessions, peak bursts up to ~1,200–1,500 concurrent sessions. Global RPS estimate initially ~150–200 RPS across regions.
- Streaming expectations: sustained token emission ~8–12 tokens/sec per stream; sessions average ~150–300 tokens.
- Regional & residency: EU personal data must stay in EU (storage + logs). APAC also prefers local residency; US traffic should stay in US.
- Compliance: SOC 2 + DPA required; legal will request residency clause in contract.

What we propose next: 
1) Technical deep-dive/POC with Rishi — validate p95 and streaming under realistic concurrency and network conditions.
2) We’ll produce an initial capacity estimate and region-specific sizing (EU/APAC/US).
3) We’ll share our SLO playbook + network checklist (attached) and a proposed routing approach (active-active regional routing with sticky sessions).

Action items: 
- Redwood: produce sizing + proposed routing and failover plan (Rishi) — target by Mon 03/09.
- Finova: share any perf test scripts / expected request size distribution + legal DPA template (Priya).
- Schedule POC kickoff (30–45m) next week to align on test harness and success criteria.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with proposed meeting slots.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: redwood-slo-playbook.pdf (see sections: regional-routing, streaming-slos, perf-test-checklist)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finova.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@finova.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 06 Mar 2026 09:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps (SLOs, routing, residency)

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side to make sure the POC targets are aligned: 

- Latency: our product team is aiming for global p95 < 700ms for first-token and p95 for completion under 1.5s for typical 150–200 token responses. First-byte is the highest priority for UX.
- Concurrency / throughput: target steady ~250 concurrent active chats (concurrent open websockets sending/receiving), with planned headroom for bursts to 1,500 concurrent. Total global peak RPS is expected to top ~300 during promos.
- Streaming rate: 10 tokens/sec average; we use server-side streaming and need consistent per-token latency to avoid stutter.
- Regional residency: EU traffic (including logs and persisted convo store) must remain in EU. APAC preference is to keep APAC traffic in APAC; if necessary and documented, some telemetry can cross borders but user content must not. This is a hard requirement for GDPR + APAC compliance teams.
- Failover: we'd like active-active routing by geography and automatic fallback to another region if a region is degraded, but only after explicit consent in the contract for data crossing and only for non-personal telemetry.

Can you confirm Redwood’s approach for active-active multi-region routing with regional KV-caches and how you handle sticky sessions? Also please send the SOC 2 / security artifact link and the DPA template so legal can start review.

If possible, we can do the POC kickoff the week of 03/09 — mornings (US) work best.

—
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering, Finova
alex.johnson@finova.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finova.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps (SLOs, routing, residency)

Alex — thanks for the clarity. A few technical notes ahead of the POC kickoff; I’ll lead the sizing and test-plan: 

1) Routing & residency model (recommended):
   - Active-active per-region deployments (US/EU/APAC) with geo-DNS + edge routing.
   - Session stickiness enforced via region cookie / JWT claim (routing key). Requests tagged with regional jurisdiction route to local cluster; fallback only for non-personal telemetry and with encryption-at-rest flagged.
   - Regional KV/cache warmers to reduce cold-start for repeated prefixes.

2) Latency & streaming:
   - We can meet first-byte p50 < 200–250ms and p95 < 600–700ms in most EU/US regions with properly sized GPU pools and local cache. APAC may need additional capacity placement (e.g., gce-asia-southeast1 / ap-northeast-1) to meet p95 targets.
   - Token emission rate (10 tps) is manageable; main risk is network RTT to region. We’ll provide a perf matrix showing median token latency vs RTT.

3) Concurrency & sizing (initial estimate for POC):
   - US (primary): reserve capacity for ~150–200 steady concurrent, burst to 900 (initial staging: 4 x A100-class GPUs equivalent).
   - EU: reserve for ~50–80 steady concurrent, burst to 300 (2 x A100 equiv).
   - APAC: reserve for ~20–50 steady concurrent, burst to 200 (1–2 x A100 equiv).
   - Cache-aware batching will reduce per-token cost and improve tail latency; we’ll tune batch window during POC.

4) Test plan & deliverables:
   - Perf harness (we’ll share the script link) to simulate websocket streams with 8–12 tps and realistic token lengths.
   - Success criteria: first-byte p95 < 700ms global, end-to-end p95 < 1.5s for 150–200 token responses under steady concurrency; graceful fallback with <2% error rate during simulated region failure.

Attaching network-topology.png (high level) and will populate the perf numbers in the shared Drive link. Please share any internal perf scripts + your expected traffic mix.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Attachment: network-topology.png

This all looks good — appreciate the concrete sizing. A couple of points from Legal/Infra: 

- Legal will need a Data Processing Addendum and a clause that any personal data for EU users remains in EU and that logs containing personal identifiers are redacted before cross-region replication. We’ll share a DPA template (Priya).
- For the POC: target test window Thursday 03/12 08:00–12:00 US-PT for an initial run. Can Redwood provide a temporary test environment in EU and APAC for us to hit?
- We’ll attach our perf matrix (finova-perf-matrix.xlsx) and a minimal test script.

Yes to the active-active approach with sticky routing and regional caches; the fallback behavior is acceptable if documented and limited to non-personal telemetry.

Next: please send available slots for Thu 03/12 morning PT for the POC kickoff and share the SOC2 artifact link.

—
Alex
